tls.title: TLS / Certificates
tls.global.hint: Global certificate verification behaviour. Configure it here for self-signed intranet services or mutual TLS.
tls.project.hint: Certificate verification for this project. Follows the global settings by default.
tls.insecure.hint: Disables chain and hostname checks. Only recommended when debugging self-signed intranet services.
tls.caCert.hint: PEM format, may contain multiple certificates; appended to the system trust store.
tls.clientCert.hint: Certificate and private key must both be provided, in PEM format.
tls.endpoint.label: Certificate check
urlEncoding.title: URL auto-encoding
urlEncoding.global.hint: Percent-encode special characters in paths and query parameters; the other four scopes may override it.
urlEncoding.project.hint: URL auto-encoding for this project. Modules, nested folders, and endpoints may override it.
urlEncoding.hint: RFC 3986 additionally encodes the space and < > " ` { } | \ ^ ' compared with WHATWG. When turned off, non-ASCII characters and hand-written %XX go out as typed — only characters that would otherwise break the request (space, control characters, and the & = # ? that split a URL) are still encoded.
wsProtocol.title: Auto-convert WebSocket protocol
wsProtocol.hint: For WebSocket endpoints only: convert a leading http:// to ws:// and https:// to wss://.
wsProtocol.global.hint: Enabled globally by default. Projects, modules, folders, and endpoints can inherit or override it.
wsProtocol.project.hint: This project follows the global setting by default; modules, folders, and endpoints can override it further.
wsProtocol.scope.hint: Children inherit this setting by default; nested folders and endpoints can override it.
request.hint: These settings apply to every request; enter 0 for no limit on the size fields.
request.timeout.hint: Global timeout at the end of the five-level chain, in milliseconds. Leave empty for 300000; enter 0 for no timeout.
request.followRedirects.hint: Follow 3xx redirects automatically; projects, modules, nested folders, and endpoints may override it.
request.noCache.hint: Add Cache-Control: no-cache to every request. A request that already sets this header is left untouched.
request.jsonComments.hint: Allow // and /* */ comments and trailing commas in JSON bodies; they are stripped before the request is sent or exported as cURL. Only applies when stripping yields valid JSON — otherwise the body is sent as-is.
request.userAgent.hint: Leave empty to send the built-in default shown in the field. An endpoint that sets its own User-Agent header wins.
request.maxResponse.hint: Bytes beyond the limit are not read and the response is marked as truncated. 0 means unlimited (a download endpoint will be read fully into memory).
request.maxStored.hint: Truncation threshold when writing response snapshots and request history, so one large response cannot bloat the database.
request.maxWSFrame.hint: Frames larger than this close the connection, preventing an oversized frame from exhausting memory.
request.maxStreamEvent.hint: Maximum bytes in one SSE event. The stream is stopped when it is exceeded; 0 means unlimited.
request.maxStream.hint: Maximum cumulative bytes read from one SSE connection. The stream is stopped when it is exceeded; 0 means unlimited.
request.maxStreamEvents.hint: Maximum events retained from one SSE connection. The stream is stopped when it is exceeded; 0 means unlimited.
request.autoReconnectSSE.hint: When an SSE response ends normally, reconnect with its latest Last-Event-ID. Disabled by default so one-shot event streams do not change behavior.
request.maxSSEReconnects.hint: Maximum automatic reconnects for one sent request. The server retry: value controls the wait; 0 disables reconnecting.
history.retention.hint: Every history row stores a full response snapshot, so without a retention policy the table grows without bound. Applied once at startup.
history.retentionDays.hint: History older than this is removed. 0 keeps it forever.
history.maxRows.hint: Oldest rows are evicted beyond this count. 0 means unlimited.
history.pruned: History pruned by the retention policy

curl.importHint: Paste a cURL command (browser DevTools' Copy as cURL works) to create an unsaved request.
postman.scriptsHint: Pre-request and test scripts are converted into endpoint scripts.
postman.moduleHint: Imported as a new module in this project; collection variables become project global variables.
import.title: Import APIs
import.hint.project: A project file exported by this app
import.file.hint: Click to choose a file, or drop one here
import.url.hint: The app fetches this URL directly — no browser CORS limits
import.match.hint.apifox: Decides what counts as the same endpoint. The source ID is Apifox's own endpoint ID, so renames and path changes are still recognised. Use the name variant when one path hosts several endpoints that differ only by name.
import.match.hint.openapi: Decides what counts as the same endpoint. The source ID is the document's operationId — an optional field, so operations without one fall back to method + path.
cookie.title: Cookie manager
cookie.hint: Modules use private cookie sessions by default. Explicitly share a session for SSO or cross-service testing. Requests still send only cookies matching the target URL.
cookie.jar.title: Named sessions
cookie.jar.hint: A session can stay private to one module or be bound to several. Existing projects keep their previous project-wide sharing after upgrade.
cookie.jar.bindingCount: Used by {{count}} module or environment bindings
cookie.binding.title: Module and environment bindings
cookie.binding.hint: A module default selects the normal request session. Each environment can inherit it, select another session, or disable automatic cookies.
runner.title: Run collection
runner.empty: Press Run to execute every endpoint in this collection
endpoint.auth.digestHint: The server answers with a 401 challenge first; the digest is computed from it and the request is resent automatically.
endpoint.auth.oauth.hint: Only grants that need no browser redirect are supported; for the authorization code flow obtain the token externally and use Bearer auth. Tokens are cached until they expire.
history.maskSensitive.hint: Masks Authorization, Cookie and API-key headers plus secret variable values. History stores long-lived credentials — a copied database file leaks them.
endpoint.body.graphql.hint: Sent as a standard GraphQL-over-HTTP JSON body. Malformed variables are ignored and the query is still sent.
update.hint: Check for and install new versions from GitHub Releases. Checks only — nothing is downloaded until you say so.
update.noChanges: This release ships no release notes.
update.autoCheck.hint: Checks periodically after launch and reports findings here.
update.prerelease.hint: Pre-releases carry unfinished features and may be unstable.
update.blocked.appimage: An AppImage cannot replace itself in place — grab the new version from the downloads page.
update.blocked.readonly: The application directory is not writable (usually a package-manager or system-directory install). Upgrade the way you installed it.
update.blocked.unknown: This environment cannot update in place — grab the new version from the downloads page.
error.update.disabled: Automatic updates are not available in this environment
error.update.not_ready: There is no update to install
data.hint: All your data lives in a single database file on this machine. Here you can see how large it is and give deleted space back to the disk.
data.reclaimable.hint: Clearing history or deleting projects only marks data as deleted — the file shrinks only after compacting.
data.export.hint: The export is a complete database file. Take it with you to a new machine and load it back with “Restore from file” below. It contains tokens and passwords in plain text — keep it as safely as a password file.
data.restore.title: Restore from backup
data.restore.hint: The app backs up automatically before an upgrade; the most recent ones are listed below. Restoring replaces all current data, and the replaced copy is kept as a backup.
data.backups.empty: No automatic backups yet (they are created only when an upgrade changes the database).
data.restore.staged: Ready — takes effect after restarting the app
data.restore.pending: A restore is queued and will take effect after you restart the app.
data.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
data.diagnostics.hint: Exports a zip with the version, platform, database size and the last few days of logs — attach it when reporting a problem. It does not include the database file (which holds tokens and passwords in plain text).
data.crash.notice: The app did not exit cleanly last time — it may have crashed. Export diagnostics and send it over; the logs from that moment are inside.
data.crash.toast: The app did not exit cleanly last time. You can export diagnostics under Settings → Data
settings.about.releases.hint: If a new version does not work for you, download any earlier one from here and install it back — your data stays put.

importexport.exportSecrets.hint: The export file is plain text. Without credentials, variable names and auth settings are still kept — only the values are left empty for the other side to fill in.
